---
title: "Did the 2019 policy change packages or the time from submission to publication?"
---

The AEA-wide data and code policy, with review by the AEA Data Editor, applies to articles published from 2019. Two outcomes are tested, separately:

- **(a) Presence of a replication package:** whether a research article has one (linear probability model). Articles from 2010 on, all AEA journals.
- **(b) Time from submission to publication:** months from submission to print publication. AER, AER:Insights, and AEJs, in the years where it can be measured (2016–2024, depending on the journal).

## Specifications

All models are OLS on articles, with standard errors clustered by journal × year of publication. Years are **years of print publication**: *post* is 1 for articles published in or after the implementation year, and trends are in publication year.

- **All journals pooled:** journal fixed effects, with and without a linear trend for each journal. For packages, also a difference in differences: P&P, JEL and JEP (no policy before 2019) against the AER and AEJs. For the time to publication, also *post* × *has package*.
- **A single journal:** with one journal, the journal fixed effect is just the intercept. The model without a trend is the difference in means before and after, and the model with a trend adds one linear trend in publication year.

The full list of specifications is in Table 6 on [Data and methods](methods.qmd).

**Placebos.** The same models are estimated with fake implementation years. Placebos at 2017 and 2018 use only years before 2019. Placebos at 2020 and 2021 use only years from 2019 on. The actual break is never inside a placebo sample. If the 2019 estimate reflects the policy, the placebo estimates should be close to zero.

## Explore by journal

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
regPkg = FileAttachment("data/regressions_packages.csv").csv({typed: true})
regDelay = FileAttachment("data/regressions_delay.csv").csv({typed: true})
viewof outcome = Inputs.radio(["Replication package (percentage points)", "Time from submission to publication (months)"],
                              {label: "Outcome", value: "Replication package (percentage points)"})
regs = outcome.startsWith("Replication") ? regPkg : regDelay
scale = outcome.startsWith("Replication") ? 100 : 1
rjournals = ["All journals", ...["AER","AER:Insights","AEA P&P","AEJ:Applied Economics","AEJ:Economic Policy",
             "AEJ:Macro","AEJ:Micro","JEL","JEP"].filter(j => regs.some(d => d.Journal === j))]
viewof rj = Inputs.select(rjournals, {label: "Journal", value: "All journals"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// with a single journal, the journal FE is the intercept: label the models accordingly
specLabels = rj === "All journals"
  ? ({its_fe: "Journal FE", its_trend: "Journal FE + journal trends", did: "DiD (year FE)",
      did_trend: "DiD + group trends", pkg: "Post × has package"})
  : ({its_fe: "Before/after (no trend)", its_trend: "Before/after + linear trend"})
rsel = regs.filter(d => d.Journal === rj).map(d => ({...d, Spec: specLabels[d.spec],
          kind: d.type === "actual" ? "Actual (2019)" : "Placebo",
          est: scale * d.estimate, lo95: scale * d.lo, hi95: scale * d.hi}))
specs = Object.values(specLabels).filter(s => rsel.some(d => d.Spec === s))
Plot.plot({
  title: `${rj}: estimated change at the actual and placebo implementation years`,
  width, height: 280 * Math.ceil(specs.length / 2), marginLeft: 50, marginTop: 30, marginBottom: 45,
  fx: {axis: null}, fy: {axis: null, padding: 0.2},
  x: {type: "point", label: "Implementation year (actual or placebo)", tickFormat: "d", domain: [2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021]},
  y: {label: outcome, grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["Actual (2019)", "Placebo"], range: ["#C2611F", "#2F6DB5"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#888"}),
    Plot.text(rsel.filter((d, i, a) => a.findIndex(e => e.Spec === d.Spec) === i),
              {fx: d => specs.indexOf(d.Spec) % 2, fy: d => Math.floor(specs.indexOf(d.Spec) / 2),
               text: "Spec", frameAnchor: "top", fontWeight: "bold", fontSize: 12, dy: -14}),
    Plot.ruleX(rsel, {x: "cutoff", y1: "lo95", y2: "hi95", stroke: "kind", strokeWidth: 2.5,
               fx: d => specs.indexOf(d.Spec) % 2, fy: d => Math.floor(specs.indexOf(d.Spec) / 2)}),
    Plot.dot(rsel, {x: "cutoff", y: "est", fill: "kind", r: 4,
             fx: d => specs.indexOf(d.Spec) % 2, fy: d => Math.floor(specs.indexOf(d.Spec) / 2),
             channels: {Years: d => `${d.first_year}–${d.last_year}`, n: "n", Clusters: "n_clusters",
                        "Pre mean": d => (scale * d.mean_pre).toFixed(1), p: d => d.p.toFixed(3)},
             tip: {format: {x: "d", fx: false, fy: false, y: d => d.toFixed(2)}}})
  ]
})
```

Estimates, confidence intervals and sample sizes for every journal are in Tables 7–10 on [Data and methods](methods.qmd).

## Reading the results

**(a) Replication packages.**

- Without trends, the 2019 estimate is positive. But the placebos before 2019 are just as large, so the share was already rising before the policy.
- With journal or group trends, nothing is left at 2019.
- P&P and JEP shares jumped around 2013–14, well before the policy.
- JEL is the exception. Its share went from under 10% before 2019 to 20–38% from 2020 on. Its 2019 estimate is +24 points without a trend (+9, not significant, with one). The significant 2020 "placebo" puts the jump in 2020, which fits the lag between acceptance under the new policy and print publication.
- AER, AEJ:Applied, AEJ:Economic Policy, and AEJ:Macro, which already had policies, were at 75–100% and flat. AEJ:Micro is lower and varies more, because many of its articles are theory papers without data.

**(b) Time from submission to publication.**

- Without trends, the time from submission to publication is about 4 months longer after 2019. But the placebos are positive too: +4 months at 2018, before the policy, and +2 to +3 at 2020–21, after it. Times rose gradually over 2017–2022; there was no single step at 2019.
- With journal trends, the 2019 estimate is small and not significant (+0.7 months). The 2020 and 2021 placebos stay at about +2.
- The change is no different for articles with a replication package.

**Caveats.**

- The policy is a single break in time, with no untreated comparison, so trends and other changes in the same years cannot be separated from it. These include COVID, a publication backlog in 2021–22, and editorial changes.
- For the time to publication, the years before 2019 are only 2016–18 (2018 for the AER). The trend models are therefore barely identified in the placebo samples before 2019: with three years, the 2017 and 2018 placebos are the same fit with opposite signs.
- Clusters are journal × year. With few years per journal, the confidence intervals of the single-journal estimates are approximate.
